ISEC_MACHINE_GROUP.description: Optional Ivanti Security Controls (iSec) machine group name that scopes which scan is processed when ISEC_SCAN_ID is not set. Machine groups are user-defined collections of managed Windows endpoints — typically friendly names like 'Workstations' / 'Servers' / 'DC Tier-1' (alphanumeric + spaces + ._- up to 128 chars). When set, the executor calls GET /api/scans?machineGroup={name} and picks the most recent scan whose machineGroup column matches case-insensitively (falling back to the most recent overall scan if no group match is found). At least one of ISEC_MACHINE_GROUP / ISEC_SCAN_ID must be set; setting both pins the executor to that specific scan and emits the machine group only in the host description for context.

ISEC_SCAN_ID.description: Optional Ivanti Security Controls (iSec) scan identifier — the integer / short alphanumeric id of a completed Patch scan whose missing-patch catalogue is pulled. Found in the iSec console under Patch -> Scan View -> select the scan (the value is the column labelled 'Scan ID') or via GET /api/scans. The executor hard-validates the identifier shape client-side (alphanumeric + ._- up to 64 chars) so a typo or control char can't fan out into '/api/scans/None' calls. At least one of ISEC_SCAN_ID / ISEC_MACHINE_GROUP must be set. When unset, the executor picks the most recent scan for the optional ISEC_MACHINE_GROUP filter.

ISEC_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional client-side severity floor for iSec missing-patch findings. Accepts info | low | medium | high | critical (plus iSec synonyms: severe -> critical, important -> high, moderate / warning -> medium, minor -> low, informational / information / unspecified -> info) plus numeric-string CVSS-style input bucketed via severity_from_cvss (<4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, >=9 critical). Patches below the floor are dropped from the Faraday output after per-patch severity normalisation (bucketed from the freeform severity string enum + numeric cvssScore 0-10 fallback). Defaults to info (no filtering).

name: ivanti_security_controls
title: Ivanti Security Controls (iSec)
description: Ivanti Security Controls (iSec) patch-management REST importer. Pulls the scan metadata record (machine group + scan template + start time + machine count + status) and the missing-patch catalogue from an iSec console via GET <ISEC_HOST>/api/scans (used when ISEC_SCAN_ID is not set — most recent scan in the optional ISEC_MACHINE_GROUP filter is picked), GET <ISEC_HOST>/api/scans/{scan_id} (scan metadata), and GET <ISEC_HOST>/api/scans/{scan_id}/missingPatches (paginated missing-patch catalogue keyed by machineId / machineName / ip plus the patch metadata — bulletinId / kbId / cveIds / severity / releaseDate / supersededBy). Each scanned machine becomes one Faraday host (keyed by the iSec machine record — hostname / IP / OS string / MAC / domain / machine group carried verbatim from the missingPatches entries) with host.os set to the iSec operatingSystem string (e.g. 'Microsoft Windows Server 2019 Standard'). Each missing patch attaches as a Faraday vulnerability with the engine prefix [PATCH-MGMT]. Severity is bucketed from the freeform severity string enum (critical / important / moderate / low / unspecified plus iSec synonyms severe / high / medium / minor / informational / information / none / unknown) with the numeric cvssScore / cvss / score / riskScore 0-10 used as a CVSS-style fallback. Status mapped from status / state / patchStatus / deploymentStatus / installStatus (missing / open / pending / new / detected / applicable / scheduled / in_progress / installing / reboot_pending -> open, installed / applied / succeeded / fixed / patched / resolved / mitigated / closed / completed / superseded / not_applicable -> closed, ignored / suppressed / deferred / excluded / waived / accepted / acknowledged / risk_accepted / will_not_install / false_positive -> risk-accepted). Pagination uses iSec's canonical page + count cursor pattern (PAGE_SIZE=100 per page capped at MAX_PAGES=200) with nextLink / @odata.nextLink + total / @odata.count exhaustion detection. Refs include iSec-Bulletin / iSec-Patch / iSec-Vendor / iSec-Product / iSec-Family / iSec-Classification / iSec-Machine pivots plus inline advisory URLs and KB references (numeric Microsoft KB ids harvested from kb / kbId / kbIds fields plus inline scans of description / summary / bulletinId / patchName — emitted as KB: KB<num> refs alongside the canonical https://support.microsoft.com/help/<num> Microsoft URL). CVE list harvested via a strict CVE-\d{4}-\d+ regex from cve / cveId / cves / cveIds plus title / summary / description / patchDescription / bulletinSummary token scans. Auth: iSec issues per-tenant API keys carried as Authorization: AppKey <ISEC_API_KEY> plus Accept: application/json on every /api/ call. ISEC_HOST is the iSec endpoint URL (http(s)://host[:port], trailing slash stripped client-side, control chars rejected). ISEC_API_KEY is the key created in the iSec console under Tools -> Options -> REST API. Tags: [ivanti, patch-management, ivanti-security-controls, missing-patch].
